resources.string: Automatically looking for local servers using service advertisements, Windows discovery and a bounded SMB2/3 scan. No login or passwords are tried. Select a server, then enter its share or collection and credentials.
Service discovery is unavailable. You can still scan for SMB or enter a server manually.
No supported IPv4 Wi-Fi/Ethernet subnet. Advertised services may still appear; otherwise enter the server manually.
Scanning nearby addresses for SMB2/3 (up to 20 seconds)…
SMB scan finished. Select a result or enter a server manually. WebDAV servers appear only if they advertise their service.
Use the full WebDAV collection URL. HTTPS is recommended; HTTP sends credentials without encryption. Files open as local copies. To save edits on the server, copy them back explicitly.
Connect to an SMB2/3 share, for example smb://192.168.1.10/Documents. A custom port can be added after the host. SMB1 is not supported.
Existing files are not overwritten. A move deletes its source only after a successful transfer. Cancellation or failure may leave a partial destination.
Deleting a folder also deletes everything inside it on the server.
Use the folder list to navigate this connection. Saved connections are available from its sidebar entry.
Nearby devices permission is required for local servers on Android 17+. Allow it in app settings, then connect again.
Extract archive entries to a local folder before copying or moving them to a network connection.
Copy FTP files to a local folder before transferring them to WebDAV or SMB.
Connect to an FTP or FTPS server. Saved FTP profiles remain available here. Files open as local copies; copy edits back explicitly.
Delete “%1$s” and remove its sidebar pin? Server files are not affected.
Saved connection not found. Add it again in Network connections.
Enter a server hostname or IP address, without a URL path
%1$s · Server does not report storage space
Creating entries in FTP panes is not supported here.
